passages.text: Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, O children of Israel, against the whole family that I brought up out of the land of Egypt: “Only you have I known from all the families of the earth; therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke a word against the people of Israel.
The LORD spoke against the whole family of Israel.
The LORD brought this family out of the land of Egypt.
The LORD says, “I have known only you among all the families of the earth.
Therefore, I will punish you for all your sins.”
passages.original: שִׁמְע֞וּ אֶת־ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה עֲלֵיכֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַ֚ל כָּל־ הַמִּשְׁפָּחָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֧ר הֶעֱלֵ֛יתִי מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרַ֖יִם לֵאמֹֽר׃ רַ֚ק אֶתְכֶ֣ם יָדַ֔עְתִּי מִכֹּ֖ל מִשְׁפְּח֣וֹת הָאֲדָמָ֑ה עַל־ כֵּן֙ אֶפְקֹ֣ד עֲלֵיכֶ֔ם אֵ֖ת כָּל־ עֲוֺנֹֽתֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Can two walk together without agreeing where to go?
passages.sermon: Two people walk together only if they agree to meet.\r\nThey do not walk together unless they have agreed.
passages.original: הֲיֵלְכ֥וּ שְׁנַ֖יִם יַחְדָּ֑ו בִּלְתִּ֖י אִם־ נוֹעָֽדוּ׃

passages.text: Does a lion roar in the forest when he has no prey? Does a young lion growl in his den if he has caught nothing?
passages.sermon:
A lion is a strong animal.
A lion lives in the forest.
A lion roars when it has caught prey.
A lion does not roar if it has no prey.
A young lion lives in its den.
A young lion growls when it has caught something.
A young lion does not growl if it has caught nothing.
passages.original: הֲיִשְׁאַ֤ג אַרְיֵה֙ בַּיַּ֔עַר וְטֶ֖רֶף אֵ֣ין ל֑וֹ הֲיִתֵּ֨ן כְּפִ֤יר קוֹלוֹ֙ מִמְּעֹ֣נָת֔וֹ בִּלְתִּ֖י אִם־ לָכָֽד׃

passages.text: Does a bird land in a snare where no bait has been set? Does a trap spring from the ground when it has nothing to catch?
passages.sermon: A bird does not land in a snare if there is no bait for it.\r\nA trap does not spring up from the ground if it has caught nothing.
passages.original: הֲתִפֹּ֤ל צִפּוֹר֙ עַל־ פַּ֣ח הָאָ֔רֶץ וּמוֹקֵ֖שׁ אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ הֲיַֽעֲלֶה־ פַּח֙ מִן־ הָ֣אֲדָמָ֔ה וְלָכ֖וֹד לֹ֥א יִלְכּֽוֹד׃

passages.text: If a ram’s horn sounds in a city, do the people not tremble? If calamity comes to a city, has not the LORD caused it?
passages.sermon:
A ram’s horn sounds in a city.
The people hear it.
The people tremble.
Calamity comes to a city.
The LORD has caused the calamity.
passages.original: אִם־ יִתָּקַ֤ע שׁוֹפָר֙ בְּעִ֔יר וְעָ֖ם לֹ֣א יֶחֱרָ֑דוּ אִם־ תִּהְיֶ֤ה רָעָה֙ בְּעִ֔יר וַיהוָ֖ה לֹ֥א עָשָֽׂה׃

passages.text: Surely the Lord GOD does nothing without revealing His plan to His servants the prophets.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD is the ruler of all.
He acts with purpose.
He does nothing in secret.
He always reveals His plan first.
He tells His plan to His servants.
His servants are the prophets.
The prophets receive His message before He acts.
passages.original: כִּ֣י לֹ֧א יַעֲשֶׂ֛ה אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה דָּבָ֑ר כִּ֚י אִם־ גָּלָ֣ה סוֹד֔וֹ אֶל־ עֲבָדָ֖יו הַנְּבִיאִֽים׃

passages.text: The lion has roared— who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken— who will not prophesy?
passages.sermon:
A lion roars.
Everyone hears the roar.
Everyone feels fear.
The Lord GOD speaks.
Everyone hears His words.
Everyone must prophesy.
passages.original: אַרְיֵ֥ה שָׁאָ֖ג מִ֣י לֹ֣א יִירָ֑א אֲדֹנָ֤י יְהוִה֙ דִּבֶּ֔ר מִ֖י לֹ֥א יִנָּבֵֽא׃

passages.text: Proclaim to the citadels of Ashdod and to the citadels of Egypt: “Assemble on the mountains of Samaria; see the great unrest in the city and the acts of oppression in her midst.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people through His prophet.
He commands a message to be announced.
Proclaim this message to the strongholds in Ashdod.
Proclaim this message to the strongholds in Egypt.
Say to them: Gather on the mountains near Samaria.
Look at Samaria.
See the great confusion inside the city.
See the many acts of oppression among the people there.
passages.original: הַשְׁמִ֙יעוּ֙ עַל־ אַרְמְנ֣וֹת בְּאַשְׁדּ֔וֹד וְעַֽל־ אַרְמְנ֖וֹת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וְאִמְר֗וּ הֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ עַל־ הָרֵ֣י שֹׁמְר֔וֹן וּרְא֞וּ מְהוּמֹ֤ת רַבּוֹת֙ בְּתוֹכָ֔הּ וַעֲשׁוּקִ֖ים בְּקִרְבָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: “For they know not how to do right,” declares the LORD. “They store up violence and destruction in their citadels.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD says the people do not know how to do what is right.
They gather violence in their strongholds.
They store up destruction in their citadels.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ יָדְע֥וּ עֲשׂוֹת־ נְכֹחָ֖ה נְאֻם־ יְהוָ֑ה הָאֽוֹצְרִ֛ים חָמָ֥ס וָשֹׁ֖ד בְּאַרְמְנֽוֹתֵיהֶֽם׃פ

passages.text: Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says: “An enemy will surround the land; he will pull down your strongholds and plunder your citadels.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks with authority and power.
He says these words.
An enemy will come.
The enemy will surround the land.
He will take away your strength.
He will destroy your strongholds.
He will plunder your citadels.
passages.original: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה צַ֖ר וּסְבִ֣יב הָאָ֑רֶץ וְהוֹרִ֤ד מִמֵּךְ֙ עֻזֵּ֔ךְ וְנָבֹ֖זּוּ אַרְמְנוֹתָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: This is what the LORD says: “As the shepherd snatches from the mouth of the lion two legs or a piece of an ear, so the Israelites dwelling in Samaria will be rescued having just the corner of a bed or the cushion of a couch.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
A shepherd sometimes saves only a small part of a sheep from a lion.
He may pull out two legs.
He may pull out a piece of an ear.
In the same way, only a small part of Israel will be saved.
The people of Israel live in Samaria.
They will escape with only a corner of a bed.
They will escape with only a cushion from a couch.
passages.original: כֹּה֮ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָה֒ כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ יַצִּ֨יל הָרֹעֶ֜ה מִפִּ֧י הָאֲרִ֛י שְׁתֵּ֥י כְרָעַ֖יִם א֣וֹ בְדַל־ אֹ֑זֶן כֵּ֣ן יִנָּצְל֞וּ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל הַיֹּֽשְׁבִים֙ בְּשֹׁ֣מְר֔וֹן בִּפְאַ֥ת מִטָּ֖ה וּבִדְמֶ֥שֶׁק עָֽרֶשׂ׃

passages.text: Hear and testify against the house of Jacob, declares the Lord GOD, the God of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD speaks.
The Lord is the God of Hosts.
He commands you to listen.
He commands you to testify against the house of Jacob.
passages.original: שִׁמְע֥וּ וְהָעִ֖ידוּ בְּבֵ֣ית יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב נְאֻם־ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י הַצְּבָאֽוֹת׃

passages.text: On the day I punish Israel for their transgressions, I will visit destruction on the altars of Bethel; the horns of the altar will be cut off, and they will fall to the ground.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is God.
The Lord is the God of Hosts.
The Lord speaks to Israel.
Israel has sinned.
The Lord will punish Israel for their transgressions.
The Lord will bring destruction on the altars at Bethel.
The horns of the altar will be cut off.
The horns will fall to the ground.
passages.original: כִּ֗י בְּי֛וֹם פָּקְדִ֥י פִשְׁעֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עָלָ֑יו וּפָֽקַדְתִּי֙ עַל־ מִזְבְּח֣וֹת בֵּֽית־ אֵ֔ל וְנִגְדְּעוּ֙ קַרְנ֣וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וְנָפְל֖וּ לָאָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: I will tear down the winter house along with the summer house; the houses of ivory will also perish, and the great houses will come to an end,” declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD will act with power.
The LORD will destroy the winter house.
The LORD will destroy the summer house.
The LORD will cause the houses of ivory to perish.
The LORD will bring an end to many great houses.
passages.original: וְהִכֵּיתִ֥י בֵית־ הַחֹ֖רֶף עַל־ בֵּ֣ית הַקָּ֑יִץ וְאָבְד֞וּ בָּתֵּ֣י הַשֵּׁ֗ן וְסָפ֛וּ בָּתִּ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס
